13: 十三点 — Shanghainese slang for "silly". Western 13 superstition also applies.
14: 要死 / 实死 — "will die / certain death".
18: 要发 / 实发 — "will prosper / sure prosperity". HK plate "18" sold for HK$16.5M.
28: 易发 (Cantonese) — "easy prosperity". HK plate "28" sold for HK$18.1M.
33: Cantonese: 生生 "life after life / growing"; Mandarin: 散散 can read as "scatter". Dialect-dependent.
38: 三八 — Women's Day (March 8) but also a common insult for a gossipy woman (三八婆). Context matters.
68: 六八 — 路发 / 禄发 "road to prosperity".
88: 发发 — double prosperity; also looks like 囍 double happiness. Online, 88 = "bye-bye".
250: 二百五 — slang for "idiot". Avoid in names, prices and gifts.
338: Cantonese folk reading 生生发 (saang saang faat) — "grow, grow, prosper". In Mandarin the embedded 三八 (38) can read as slang, so this one is dialect-dependent.
514: 吾要死 — can read as "I want to die" in slang; avoided.
520: 我爱你 — "I love you" (May 20 is China's internet Valentine's Day).
521: 我愿意 / 我爱你 — "I'm willing / I love you".
1314: 一生一世 — "one life, one world", forever.
1688: 一路发发 — "prosperity all the way, doubled".
3344: 生生世世 — "life after life", eternal (sound-alike overrides the 4s here).
8888: Quadruple prosperity — among the most prized endings.
5201314: 我爱你一生一世 — "I love you for a lifetime". The ultimate romantic code.
00: 00 — the international dialling prefix in China; also "00后", China's post-2000 generation.
